title: Full Supabase: backend auth cutover
description: Replace Firebase token verification and auth bootstrap in backend services with Supabase-compatible auth for the full-supabase branch. Scope includes FastAPI dependencies, websocket auth, agent-proxy auth, and any server-issued token/session flows that currently depend on Firebase.
notes:
Removed direct Firebase imports from backend auth-critical entrypoints in the full-supabase branch. agent-proxy now verifies bearer tokens through providers.auth and reads/writes agent VM metadata plus chat/session history via shared repositories instead of firebase_admin/firestore. routers/agent_tools now updates VM state through database.users instead of Firestore-only code paths. Also normalized Supabase JWT claims to expose uid alongside sub for compatibility with existing auth dependencies.
Also removed direct Firebase app initialization from backend/pusher/main.py by routing service startup through providers.startup, so pusher now follows the shared backend-mode bootstrap path too.
Removed Firebase-only startup from backend/modal/job.py by switching it to providers.startup, and dropped the stale Firestore import from backend/database/helpers.py. Remaining non-firebase-specific runtime blockers are now mainly google-cloud based translation/speaker-sample code rather than firebase_admin/firestore bootstrapping.

title: Full Supabase: storage cutover

title: Full Supabase: repository migration core domains

notes: Started the first real Supabase/Postgres repository slice instead of placeholder-only facades. Added database.supabase.users and database.supabase.chat with JSONB-backed user profile / agent VM, chat session, and chat message persistence plus compatibility normalization for app_id/plugin_id and enhanced-protection chat text. Added bootstrap SQL for user_profiles, chat_sessions, and chat_messages in backend/supabase/0001_user_profiles_and_chat.sql, and wired database.users/database.chat facades to load these partial Supabase implementations.

title: Decision: dedicated full-supabase cutover branch
description: The user chose to proceed with a dedicated full-supabase branch/worktree rather than constraining the work to the smallest upstreamable dual-backend PR. This branch is expected to remove Firebase runtime dependencies entirely for the target deployment path and can accept broader changes to backend, app, web, desktop, and local infra in service of a coherent self-host stack built around Supabase and pgvector.

title: Decision: dual backend with Firebase default, Supabase self-host option, pgvector
description: Architecture decision from planning: upstream-friendly approach is to preserve the existing Firebase path as the default while adding an optional Supabase-backed self-host mode. Do not attempt to fully emulate Firestore or Firebase wire protocols on top of Supabase. Instead, add provider interfaces at the real seams: auth verification/session issuance, storage/blob operations, vector storage, and selected domain repositories. Use pgvector as the default vector backend for the Supabase/self-host route to minimize moving parts. Goal is a PRable change set that minimizes churn for existing users while enabling individuals to self-host without standing up Pinecone/Qdrant plus Firebase cloud infra.
notes:
Supabase/self-host mode must not depend on Firebase at runtime. Treat this as a hard boundary, not just a dormant code path.
Subsequent user pivot: proceed on a dedicated full-supabase branch for the full cutover effort. This decision remains useful as a contrast against the upstream-minimal option, but active implementation may now optimize for the dedicated branch rather than PR-minimal scope.

Qdrant work from the hybrid branch can inform the abstraction, but pgvector should be the primary target for the upstreamable self-host path.

title: Design dual-backend auth, data, and storage layer (Firebase default, Supabase self-host)
description: Design the smallest viable abstraction layer that keeps Firebase as the default upstream backend while allowing an optional Supabase/local Supabase route for self-hosting. Scope includes auth token verification/session handling, data persistence seams, and blob storage. Prefer targeted adapters and repository boundaries over attempting to emulate Firestore on top of Supabase. Deliver a PRable migration design that minimizes churn in existing clients and backend modules while defining which Firestore-heavy domains move first.
notes: Design target tightened: Supabase mode must be Firebase-free at runtime. Authentication, storage, and data access need real provider swaps, not wrappers around Firebase clients.

title: Audit current/local Omi infra and plan Supabase + provider migration
description: User requested: initialize this repo against the centralized local beads/Dolt server, inspect this open-source Omi repo and the local running fork at ../../omi, and produce a concrete migration/gap plan for: (A) replacing Firebase-backed infra with Supabase/local Supabase support, (B) adding local TTS (NVIDIA Parakeet) plus ElevenLabs while preserving Deepgram paths, (C) allowing a small local LLM initial pass, (D) supporting OpenRouter alongside OpenAI/Anthropic, and (E) allowing local embeddings via transformers or a local model endpoint alongside existing API embeddings. Scope includes identifying what already exists in ../../omi (especially OpenRouter), what can be cherry-picked or pulled forward, and what remains to build in this repo. Deliverable is a self-contained implementation plan with concrete code areas and dependency ordering.
notes:
User clarified preferred target: keep Firebase as the default upstream path, add an optional Supabase self-host route, use pgvector to minimize moving parts, and optimize for an upstreamable PR with minimal backend swap churn for end users self-hosting individually.
Hard requirement from user: when running in Supabase mode, there must be no Firebase dependency at runtime.
Pivot approved by user on 2026-04-20: create and use a dedicated full-supabase branch/worktree for a full Firebase-free Supabase cutover instead of limiting the initial effort to an upstream-minimal dual-backend PR.
